questions.question: Define production and identify the inputs, process and outputs for a bakery.
questions.expected_answer: Production is the creation of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants. Bakery inputs: flour, yeast, water, salt, labour, ovens, electricity, management. Process: mixing, kneading, rising, baking. Output: bread (and other baked goods).

questions.question: Name the four factors of production and the reward each earns.
questions.expected_answer: Natural resources/land: rent. Labour: wages and salaries. Capital: interest. Entrepreneurship: profit.

questions.question: Describe the three sectors of production with one South African example each, and explain how they are linked.
questions.expected_answer: Primary: takes from nature (farming, mining, fishing, forestry), e.g. platinum mining. Secondary: processes raw materials into goods (manufacturing, construction, electricity), e.g. car factory. Tertiary: provides services (trade, transport, banking, education, tourism), e.g. supermarket. Linked in production chains, e.g. cotton farm → clothing factory → clothing shop.
